Ben / Jordan — apologies for the slightly long note, but wanted to be concrete so we can move fast. Attached is my draft note + annotated redlines. TL;DR options we should present to Novacorp:

Option A (Preferred commercial/legal compromise)
- Redwood: agree to defend & indemnify Novacorp for third-party IP claims specifically attributable to Redwood-provided model outputs, limited to Customer's authorized use and excluding customer-supplied prompts/materials.
- Conditions: Customer must provide notice within 30 days of claim discovery (we can negotiate 30–60 but 30 is reasonable), provide requested logs/samples, and allow Redwood to control defense (with customer participation rights).
- Caps/limits: Liability cap = 2x fees in prior 12 months; insurance offset permitted; Redwood may seek contribution from third parties.

Option B (Defensive posture / lower risk)
- Redwood: defend-only plus indemnity limited to proven Redwood-derivative infringement (we propose a narrowly-tailored definition tied to model training provenance and forensic markers).
- Cap: same 2x fees cap; include time-limited obligation (claims to be brought within 12 months of alleged act).

Key legal callouts / risk notes
- Outputs risk: AI-output infringement claims are nascent; broad defend obligations expose Redwood to downstream unknowns. Narrow triggers reduce exposure and are defensible.
- Evidence & triage: we need: request id, model id/version, input prompt, sample output, timestamps, and logs for 30–90 days. Propose a 30-day triage window before indemnity payment obligation.
- Escrow / remediation: we can offer escrow for code artifacts only if procurement insists (operationally heavy). Insurance offset language (allowing our insurance to be credited against damages) is a must for us.

Practical negotiation language to send (short paragraph):
"Redwood is prepared to agree to defend and indemnify Novacorp for third-party IP claims arising from Redwood-generated outputs that are not materially based on customer-supplied proprietary inputs, subject to (i) prompt notice, (ii) Redwood control of the defense with customer participation, (iii) a liability cap equal to two times the fees paid in the prior 12 months, and (iv) standard insurance offset and contribution rights."

Attachments: KL_comments_Novacorp_indemnity_20260908.docx (legal redlines + 1-page option memo)

If Procurement pushes for broader language, escalate to Emily (VP Sales) for exec review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
